axis.poly_variable: t = (r - r_root) / (r_tip - r_root), numpy.polyval order (highest first)
axis.derivation: for each station the aft offset is solved (bisection) so the highest point of the stowed section is flush with the hull (proud 0); lead is the per-station optimum (golden section) that minimises the flush pocket depth, then fitted by polynomials and iterated with the section planes (they depend on d aft/ds)

fold_choice.reason: stowed depth and keep-out barely change with fold (the axis re-solves); the fold angle mostly sets the deployed cone (+1 deg cone per +1 deg fold). 90 deg gives a mean cone close to the BEM nominal 12 deg with the tip bending forward; see fold_study

stowed_max_over_hull.note: highest point of each stowed part above the hull envelope (normal); design value 0 (flush), residual = solver tolerance

pocket_depth.note: radial depth below the hull of the pocket floor (blade inner surface - clearance 0.3 under the aero span, 0.8 under the root, side clearance 0.8); keepout_r = floor - MIN_WALL along the hull normal = the largest radius internal parts may use under a pocket. Half-width is about az_center (relative to the blade azimuth).

pocket_summary.floor_print_rule: both shells print +x down; the floor may rise at most tan(45 deg) per mm going forward (printable_floor), so the root-notch ramp and the pocket's forward end are cut as <= 45 deg ramps, no supports

hub_slot.note: hinge-plane coords of blade 0 (r_e along e_r, tau along the pin), swept root over fold 0..stowed in 1 deg steps, + run clearance; cut the hub and the spinner to this per blade

concept: Hub (printed, rotating): body of revolution from the hub front (static tail end + HUB_GAP) to the shaft end, outer surface = hull - spinner wall - gap. Bore 8 mm close-running with a D-flat; one M3 cup-point grub (ISO 4029) radial on the D-flat, between two blades.
Clevis per blade: the blade root ends in a full-width knuckle (cylinder about the pin) that sits in a slot between two hub ears; the 3 mm pin runs TANGENTIALLY through ear, knuckle, ear.

Pins: ISO 8734 parallel pins pressed into the ears (printed 3.0 hole), knuckle bore 3.0 + CLEAR_ROTATE. They go in along e_t through a 3 mm channel from the hub core surface; the spinner shell covers both channel ends and retains the pins (folding-prop practice).
Deployed stop: a heel tab under the knuckle; under thrust its leading face lands on the hub front ring (stop face at x = hinge_x - heel_t/2), which takes the flapwise moment.

Spinner (printed, rotating): 1.2 mm shell from the hub front to the blunt tip with three slots (slot table). Slides on from aft, keys on the slots, and is held by one axial M3 screw into a tapped hole in the shaft end; the hub's aft face bears on the spinner's inner aft wall, so rotor thrust goes hub -> spinner -> M3 screw -> shaft (the grub only locks rotation and holds the hub during assembly).
Detents: N52 4x2 magnet pairs, heel face <-> stop face (deployed) and root inner face <-> boss on the static notch floor (stowed). No springs.

grub.note: radial M3 tapped hole (2.5 drill) at an azimuth between two blades; clearance = hole axis to swept root surface minus the 1.25 mm drill radius

pin.standard: ISO 8734 parallel pin 3 x 22 (VERIFY stock length)
pin.retention: spinner shell covers both channel ends

spinner.retention: axial M3 screw into a tapped hole in the shaft end (M3 tap, 8 deep)
spinner.slot: per blade: hub_slot table (x, slot floor r_e, half-width tau) + run clearance

hub.loads_source: blade_design.json: layout_axis_check (hinge 116, 14, solved curved axis); torque from performance.envelope_up_to_runaway
hub.load_note: ESTIMATES, first-order statics: stop force = flap moment / stop lever; pin reaction = stop force + blade thrust (same direction); stresses on projected areas. Compare with PETG/PLA strength in the report; the 2.5 m/s case is the BEM worst case.

detents.magnet: 4 x 2 mm N52 disc, axial (MAGNET in params.py)
detents.per_blade: 2 in the blade (heel face, root inner face), 1 in the hub stop face, 1 in the static tail notch floor; 12 in total
detents.polarity: every pair attracting; all blades identical, all hub and all tail magnets identical

rows.source: https://www.jc-magnetics.com/Magnet-N52-4mm-2mm-Discs; 1.03 lb (jc) / 0.91 lb (https://themagnetbaron.com/collections/4mm-disc-magnets), magnet to steel plate
https://www.jc-magnetics.com/Magnet-N52-4mm-2mm-Discs; 1.03 lb (jc) / 0.91 lb (https://themagnetbaron.com/collections/4mm-disc-magnets), magnet to steel plate

calibration.note: k_design = lowest 4x2 catalogue pull / model; applied to every model force

detents.note: Forces: surface-charge model scaled by k (catalogue pull / model). Contact faces are plastic; magnets sit magnet_recess below them. A weaker stowed hold for flow-opening in water: deepen the recesses (see force_vs_gap).

blade_mass.note: ESTIMATE: solid PLA (1.24 g/cm3, same assumption as the BEM study); worst-case gravity moment about the pin = m g x cg distance from the pin axis

interference.criteria: static tail: swept blade never below the pocket floor (floor already includes 0.3/0.8 clearance); ears: no blade point in the pin + 2 mm zone; neighbours >= 1 mm at any fold pair; deployed blades apart; heel inside the spinner at both ends; deployed aero span above the hull

selection.rule: feasible: pin cover in hub core >= 2, stowed heel >= 0.5 inside the spinner, heel face >= magnet D + 0.6, stop block >= magnet H + recess + MIN_WALL + 0.6, ear clear >= 0.5, neighbour >= 1, swept root >= ROOT_CLEAR from the static tail, hub wall >= MIN_WALL; then max of the smallest margin (pin cover, heel, magnet room), ties to the smallest hinge-to-static-tail offset (front 10 only adds keep-out the internal layout does not need)

oring.groove_form: aft flank radial; tip-side (forward) flank 45 deg from the groove bottom up to the spigot OD, so the spigot prints tip-up without support
oring.guidance: Apple Rubber static radial table for cs 2.62: depth 2.03-2.18, width 3.56, squeeze 14-25 %, diametral clearance <= 0.13; globaloring: fill 60-85 %, stretch <= 5 %. Worst cases include +-0.10 mm print error on each diameter and full eccentricity. 0.20 mm diametral clearance exceeds the 0.13 table limit, which guards extrusion under pressure: acceptable at < 0.1 bar

bayonet.lip_underside: 45 deg chamfer from the seal bore in to the lip (overhang when the front shell prints equator-down)
bayonet.detent: 2 magnet pairs (N52 4x2) in the equator faces, in two of the lands between pockets; they attract at lock. Hard stop = the channel end wall, reached when the pockets of both shells align

strength.basis: tow design load passes eye -> front shell -> lugs -> aft shell; interlayer adhesion used as a shear proxy, util < 0.5 required

loads.basis: T = 0.5 rho pi R^2 v^2 C_T with C_T 0.8 at 2.5 m/s (task rule); BEM cross-check from data/blade_design.json; hull drag C_D 0.10 on the frontal area (ESTIMATE)

eye.type: printed ring at the nose tip, on the axis, ring plane = XZ (hole axis Y)
eye.plane_why: with the hole axis along Y the shackle pin runs along Y and the shackle body lies in the XY plane, so the gland under the nose (theta 180) stays clear of it

shackle_envelope.model: ESTIMATE, 5 mm stainless D-shackle: from the hole's aft edge forward, |y| <= 12 (pin), |z| <= 5

eye.print: front shell prints nose-up: the ring stands vertical on the nose plug, hole printed as a 45 deg teardrop
eye.note: legs load the layers in tension (weakest direction) and still sit far below the Prusament interlayer adhesion; use a stainless shackle or a thimble, not a bare rope, to keep the bearing stress low. v2 pull test >= design load

nose_plug.rule: inner wall |dr/dx| = 1 is the 45 deg overhang limit when printed nose-up; forward of it the cavity is filled (infill) and closed by a 38.6 mm bridge
nose_plug.alternative: leave the dome open: no supports either, but the hidden inner ceiling forward of x_45 sags (overhang up to 90 deg at the apex)

gland.seat_model: raised D18 seat block outside the hull: a cylinder on the gland axis from the hull up to the spot face, whose centre stands 3.0 mm off the hull along the axis; the M12x1.5 bore is tapped through the block, the 2.4 mm shell wall and the infilled nose plug; no boss stands in the open nose cavity
gland.axis: outer surface normal turned 10 deg toward -X (points forward-down, 33.3 deg from the hull axis)
gland.thread_engagement_rule: every generatrix of the M12 major diameter keeps >= 75 % of the 8 mm gland thread in solid material (seat block, wall, plug) before it opens into the cavity
gland.seat_note: the D18 spot face is flat and lifted on a curved nose: its rim stands up to 6.8 mm proud of the hull (a raised seat block); printed nose-up, the block's side and the bore lean 33 deg from vertical (limit 45)
gland.placement_rule: search seat x 3-12 mm (step 0.25), tilt -10 to 30 deg (step 2.5) and seat lift 0-6 mm (step 0.5), in order of the seat rim height above the hull; keep the first height where: thread engagement >= 75 % on every generatrix, seat block and bore ceiling <= 45 deg overhang, block and bore (cable exit) >= 1.0 mm ahead of the carrier plate and its ring, gland body >= 2.0 mm from the eye ring and the shackle envelope; then the larger engagement (8177 candidates, 1771 evaluated; rejected: bore_overhang 294, engagement 1428, overhang 0, carrier 2, tow 46)

previous_x12.note: the merge's boss at x 12 on the surface normal ran through the carrier plate into the bay

previous_round3.note: round 3 moved the seat to x 6 (tilt 17.5) and cleared the carrier, but its D16 thread boss hung in the nose cavity aft of the plug bridge: a 71 deg overhang printing nose-up; without that boss its thread kept only 4.25 mm

gland.seal: flat NBR washer under the gland head (IP68 with the extra O-ring, hardware.json)
gland.thread_form: tapped M12x1.5 through the seat block, the wall and the nose plug (or a printed thread), no inner locknut; the bore opens into the cavity through the plug's bridge face and the wall
gland.cable_route: gland -> nose cavity (slack loop) -> notch in the carrier rim at theta 180 -> motor leads behind the carrier

cable_notch.note: the cable lies in the notch, inside the shell's carrier ring, and turns with the carrier through the 30 deg lock twist; leave a slack loop (~120 mm, ESTIMATE) in the nose cavity

1_m_s.basis: CubeMars GL40 KV70 load line (BEM, capped point)

1.5_m_s.basis: CubeMars GL40 KV70 load line (BEM, capped point)

2.5_m_s.basis: CubeMars GL40 KV70 load line (BEM, capped point)

roll.Q_scaling: on the GL40 load line the operating TSR rises with flow (TSR 5.00 at 1 m/s, TSR 5.75 at 1.5 m/s, TSR 6.03 at 2.5 m/s), so Q does not grow with v^2 like the fin lift: Q(1.0) / Q(1.5) = 0.523 against (1.0 / 1.5)^2 = 0.444, Q(2.5) / Q(1.5) = 2.702 against 2.778 (the 2.5 m/s point is held by the cavitation cap). A fixed fin set matched at 1.5 m/s therefore under-balances at 1.0 m/s and over-balances at 2.5 m/s (balance below)

bridle.eyes: two eyes at +-Y on the nose
bridle.model: k = T a^2 / L (legs carry T/2 each)

roll.conclusion: fins carry the mean torque; nothing on an axial tow line restores roll, and the pendulum (near-neutral hull) is negligible, so any mismatch turns into a slow hull roll that twists the cable. v2 should add a roll reference: a two-leg bridle on two nose eyes (numbers above) or a cable swivel/slip ring
roll.freewheel_note: with no electrical load Q ~ 0 and the fins roll the hull the other way at p ~ tau_fin / damping (50 rpm at 1.5 m/s); v2 must keep a load on the generator (the load line above, a dump load when the battery is full)

assembly.action: Press the 688 down the tube from the open equator end, through the 608 seat (22) and the 18 mm bore, onto the seal shoulder (ID 12.5). Use a draw bolt (M6 rod, washers) through the tail end, not a hammer.
assembly.check: 688 OD 16 < 18 mm bore: passes. Seat depth 34 mm below the tube mouth: draw bolt needed. OK

assembly.action: v2: press the lip seal into the 16 mm bore from the tail end face, main lip facing aft, onto the same shoulder.
assembly.check: seal bore open aft, recessed 0.5 mm. OK

assembly.action: Press the 608 into the front seat onto its 18 mm shoulder (same draw bolt).
assembly.check: both shoulders face forward, so no retaining rings; the tube prints tail-down and both shoulders print as floors. OK

assembly.action: Slide the shaft in from the front through 608, 688 and the seal (chamfered end; a thin sleeve over the flat while it passes the seal lip).
assembly.check: the flat and the ring groove pass the seal lip: needs the chamfer and a sleeve. FLAG for the prototype

assembly.action: Fit claw B on the forward shaft end against the 608 inner race; retaining ring in its groove; tighten the 2 grub screws on the flat (1.5 mm hex key).
assembly.check: claw B sits x 52.5-63.0: its front 5.0 mm stand ahead of the equator face, inside the spigot (tip x 43.6); the spigot bore D55.9 gives radial access for a short 1.5 mm key. OK

assembly.action: Rotor (layout_rotor): blades into the hub clevis slots, 3 x 22 pins pressed into the ears through their tangential channels; hub onto the D-flat with a 0.6 mm feeler in the hub gap, M3 grub tightened; spinner slid on from aft (keys on the slots, covers the pin channels), M3 screw into the tapped shaft end.
assembly.check: hub front x 108.6, shaft end x 128.0; rotor thrust: hub -> spinner -> M3 screw -> shaft -> claw B -> 608. OK

assembly.action: v2: bond the ballast tray (if any) in the bottom sector between the ribs.
Grease the ISO 3601 / AS568 -141 and roll it into the spigot groove; glue the 2 joint magnets.
assembly.check: stretch 2.5 % nominal (1.4-3.6 % worst) in the groove; on the way the ring rolls over the lugs and the forward land (D63.89), a momentary 9 % stretch from its 58.42 ID (elastomer elongation limit not sourced; a smooth 45 deg lead-in on the lugs helps). OK

assembly.action: Tap the M12x1.5 seat (raised block at x 8.8, bottom) square to its spot face, then screw the gland in with its washer; pass the cable in and out through the open equator end, leaving ~120 mm (ESTIMATE) inside for the slack loop.
assembly.check: nothing of the gland or its seat stands in the cavity: the bore (cable exit) ends 2.27 mm ahead of the carrier plate and 1.07 mm ahead of its ring, so the carrier never meets it; thread engagement >= 6.05 mm; wrench SW 15 on the outside. OK

assembly.action: Bench: bolt the motor base to the carrier (4 x M3 on PCD 24.00, heads in counterbores on the carrier front face), fit claw A, lay the cable in the 7.5 mm rim notch at theta 180 and solder it to the motor leads.
assembly.check: all screws reachable on the bench; notch 5.5 mm from the nearest counterbore. OK

assembly.action: Push carrier + motor into the front shell through the socket (the cable slack folds into the nose cavity), tabs through the ring notches, twist 30 deg until it clicks.
assembly.check: motor D46.5 passes the socket lip D61.1; the cable lies in the notch inside the carrier ring and turns with the carrier; the generator reaction torque drives the tabs into their hard stop. OK

assembly.action: Align the entry marks, push the shells together (the claws find each other on the V lead-in; turn the rotor by hand if the dogs sit tip to tip), twist 35 deg to the stop; the magnets click.
assembly.check: the spigot (bore D55.9) slides over the aft 2.9 mm of the bay envelope (D50): 2.7 mm radial clearance. Claw engagement is blind: self-finding with the V lead-in and a free rotor. FLAG for the prototype

assembly.action: Slide each fin aft onto its rail to the stop, set the grub screw. Remove for transport. To stow the blades, turn the rotor to its index (blades over their pockets) first, then fold.
assembly.check: at the index the folding blades clear the fins by >= 2.0 mm; at other azimuths they can touch. FLAG for the user guide

assembly.action: Reverse order. The 608 comes out by pushing the shaft from the tail (claw B drives it), the 688 with a drift from the tail after the seal.
assembly.check: 688 is behind the seal: remove the seal first (it is destroyed; spare). OK

generator_bay.frontier_note: the bay runs from the carrier (needs r >= 23.37 mm for the PCD 38.14 adapter, so x_fwd >= 22.50) to the rotor face, which may not pass x 46.50 (bearing span >= 32 mm): hence L <= 24. D_max is set by the nose wall and the carrier ring (it overhangs the bay by 1.2 mm) at the bay's forward end (socket lip D 61.09 is not binding); the spigot bore (D 55.88) only matters aft of the spigot tip (x 43.59)

bearings.why: 608 in the wide front where it takes the thrust; 688 in the narrow tail under the deepest pockets; stepped bore (22 -> 18 -> 16) so both press in from the front and the 688 passes through the 608 seat; seal bore 16 = 688 bore (one reamed diameter)

criteria.note: span / overhang is reported against the 1.25 rule of thumb only; it cannot be met with the static tail at x 108 and the coned rotor (load plane x 136.3)

bearings.load_basis: tow case: T = 0.5 rho A v^2 C_T (C_T 0.8, 2.5 m/s); radial load 10 % of T and one blade 20 % off its share of T (both ESTIMATES)
bearings.location: 608 locating: claw B (thrust collar, 2 M3 grub screws on a shaft flat + a retaining-ring groove, VERIFY with the shaft supplier) bears on the 608 inner race for +X thrust; outer race on the 18 mm tube shoulder. 688 floating (slip fit on the shaft). -X handling loads close the hub gap

tube.ribs: 3 radial ribs 2.0 mm thick under the pocket floors (theta = pocket angles), from the tube front to the tail end wall; the sectors between them stay free (ballast tray in the bottom one)

seal.name: TC 8x16x5
seal.note: v1 display: pocket only, seal optional

shaft.stock: 8 mm g6/h6 stainless ground rod (hardware study: hardened 440C for the lip seal); two flats (claw B; hub D-flat 0.5 deep under the M3 grub at x 111.6), one retaining-ring groove ahead of claw B and an M3 x 8 tapped hole in the aft end (spinner screw, carries the rotor thrust), ordered machined; chamfer both ends

coupler.type: two-dog claw coupling, V lead-in, 1.0 mm axial float, 0.3 mm radial clearance per dog: engages blind as the shells close and tolerates shell-to-shell misalignment, so the motor's own bearings and the 608/688 pair are never forced into line (no 4-bearing shaft)

tube_mouth.note: the rotating claw B steps down to OD 20 over its last 2 mm, so it runs 0.95 mm clear of the static 608 seat bore where it enters the tube mouth

coupler.claw_A_mount: v2: on the bell face holes if the motor has them (unconfirmed for the GM4108H), else on an 8 mm steel stub bonded into the motor's hollow shaft (ID 8) with retaining compound; display: printed replica
coupler.thrust_collar: Ruland MSC-8-SS (bore 8, OD 16, width 8, 303 SS; hardware.json shaft_retention) inside claw B, 0.5 mm shim washer to the 608 inner race

fins.section: clarky (flat lower surface, t/c 0.117), printed flat, no supports
fins.polars: NeuralFoil large, n_crit 5, cached in out/work/layout_internal/polars_fin.json
fins.layout: identical parts at theta 93 and 273 (diametrically opposite, 3 deg off +-Y so the yawed rail pads clear the asymmetric pockets); each fin and its rail pad are yawed by the incidence about the radial line through the pivot at 0.15 c, TE toward -theta; the second fin is the first turned 180 deg about X, so the lifts are opposite and form a pure couple
fins.torque_sense: rotor omega +X: the generator reaction turns the hull the same way (+X), so the +Y fin lifts toward -Z and the -Y fin toward +Z (fin couple -X)

torque_basis.basis: CubeMars GL40 KV70 load line (BEM, capped point)
torque_basis.source: data/blade_design.json generator_coupling_estimate.load_line_by_flow (recommended generator, final blade, 'capped' point = best net power with the cavitation cap)
torque_basis.margin_reason: +10 % over the load-line torque: NeuralFoil polars are smooth-surface, and a printed Clark Y at Re ~55 k tends to give less lift; the GL40 drag torque (0.0248 N m in the BEM model) is an estimate. Lift shortfall is the likelier error, so the bias is deliberate; if the prototype over-balances, a trim fin with less incidence corrects it
torque_basis.old_rule_note: the merge sized the fins for Q = Cp 0.35 at TSR 4 (0.282 N m at 1.5 m/s), 1.60 x the load-line torque

trim.how: print fin variants whose root tongue is turned +-1 deg about the yaw pivot relative to the chord: the shell's yawed pad and groove stay, the incidence changes by +-1 deg (8 % of the torque per degree); the fin box moves by at most 0.59 mm at its far end, inside the fold clearance

yaw.offset_sign: + = toward +theta, at the hull, from the fin angle line
yaw.x_extent_note: the yawed root chord spans x 16.37-55.50 (c cos i)

fins.root_note: lift bends the fin about its chord; printed flat, the span-wise bending stress lies in the layer plane (XY strength)

rail.type: half dovetail (flat on the fin's flat side, 45 deg flank on the other): male tongue on the fin root, female groove (mean width 6, depth 4) in a 10 mm raised pad on the front shell; the pad is yawed with the fin, so the rail runs along the fin chord
rail.pad_aft_end: runs down to the equator face (x 57.5): the front shell prints on that face, so the pad's aft end stands on the bed (a 45 deg chamfer from the rail stop would need 7.1 mm, past the equator)
rail.retention: the fin slides aft onto the end stop at x 55.5 (drag pushes it home); one M3 grub screw in a heat-set insert for handling

stowed_pockets.model: yawed pad footprint (pad_footprint, 0.25 mm x 11 samples; planar pad walls meet the hull at theta + asin(lat / R)) vs each pocket's theta span at the sample x, arc at the hull radius

fold_at_index.rule: blades fold at the stowing index (blade i at psi 120 i), fold 0 to 90 deg in 1 deg steps, rotor surface from hydroegg.layout
fold_at_index.sampling: aero and shank surfaces densified to 1 mm, fold in 1 deg steps (clearances +- ~0.5 mm)
fold_at_index.model: 3D distance to the yawed pad box (|w| <= 5, up to the pad top) and fin box (|w| <= t/2, root line to tip) in the yawed frame

clearance.te_rule: index: TE at the rail end stop 2.0 mm ahead of the equator; the blades fold only at the stowing index (the pockets need it) and clear the fins by >= 2.0 mm there (fold_at_index); folding at another rotor azimuth with the fins on can touch a fin (fins come off for transport)
clearance.rule: yawed rail pad >= 2.0 mm (arc) from any pocket edge

fins.selection: smallest fin-tip diameter (handling, stowage) among fins whose couple at 1.5 m/s is 1.10-1.155 x the GL40 load-line torque (CL <= 0.75 CLmax_3D at 1/1.5/2.5 m/s) AND whose yawed pads / fins clear the pockets and the blades folding at the stowing index; candidates evaluated in that order; the least-area feasible fin is listed for comparison

model.rotor: blades from layout_rotor.json blade_mass (solid, incl. knuckle and heel); hub + spinner = hull envelope from the hub front to the tip minus what floods (hub_wet: 3 blade slots 11.7 cc, screw-access bore 0.9 cc, spinner gap 0.5 cc)
model.sealed: displacement counts the sealed static hull (minus the wet pockets), the fin rail pads outside the hull (minus their wet grooves), and the outer volume of the rotor parts and fins (closed perimeters trap the infill air)

breakdown.name: gland seat block (raised D18 outside the hull, minus the M12 bore)
fin rail pads x2 (outside the hull, minus the wet groove)
tail end block (seal boss, notch floors, magnet seats)
hub + spinner (envelope minus 3 blade slots, screw access bore, shell gap)
blades x3 (layout_rotor.json blade_mass, solid incl. knuckle and heel)
magnets x12 (rotor detents: 6 blade, 3 hub stop, 3 tail notch)
gland seat block (raised D18 outside the hull, minus the M12 bore)
fin rail pads x2 (outside the hull, minus the wet groove)
tail end block (seal boss, notch floors, magnet seats)
hub + spinner (envelope minus 3 blade slots, screw access bore, shell gap)
blades x3 (layout_rotor.json blade_mass, solid incl. knuckle and heel)
magnets x12 (rotor detents: 6 blade, 3 hub stop, 3 tail notch)

v2_needs.option_note: 4-perimeter (1.6 mm) shells first, then a small foam float on the tether for the rest (option_combined); ballast only after that, because the hull is already near neutral

trim.slack_water: near-neutral, CG 3.8 mm ahead of CB: in still water it settles nose-down; in current the rotor thrust aligns it with the flow (angle above)

roll_pendulum.note: compare with the generator torque in roll.torque: the pendulum is two orders of magnitude too weak, the fins must carry the torque

v2_ballast.where: bottom sector of the aft shell (theta 180) between the ribs at 120 and 240 deg, shot in epoxy in a printed tray; trim by sliding it along x

hardware.name: magnets x12 (rotor detents: 6 blade, 3 hub stop, 3 tail notch)

ROTOR_HUB.slot_table: data/layout_rotor.json hub_slot (cut per blade, hinge-plane coords)

DETENTS.magnet: 4 x 2 mm N52 disc, axial (MAGNET in params.py)

POCKETS.tables: data/layout_rotor.json pocket_depth (x, depth, floor_r, keepout_r, az_lo, az_hi per x; theta = -psi)

BEARING_TUBE.seat_note: printed seats = nominal D + 2 x PRESS_FIT; the 18 mm bore between the seats lets the 688 pass through the 608 seat

ribs.rule: radial ribs under the pocket floors, tube to shell

TAIL_END_BLOCK.note: solid ring: seal shoulder, seal bore, the 3 notch floors and the stowed-detent magnet seats (layout_rotor.json detents.stowed)

ORING_EQUATOR.name: ISO 3601 / AS568 -141
ORING_EQUATOR.flank: aft flank radial, tip-side flank 45 deg

FIN.retention: M3 grub in a heat-set insert

GLAND.note: seat block = D18 cylinder on the gland axis from the spot face down to the hull; bore tapped M12x1.5 through block, wall and nose plug

proposed_param_updates.HINGE_X_reason: rotor hinge sweep: only feasible HX with comfortable margins (117: 0.05 mm pin cover, 118 fails)

proposed_param_updates.KNUCKLE_L_reason: new: knuckle length along the pin (clevis slot 14.6)
proposed_param_updates.HUB_EAR_T_reason: new: hub ear thickness along the pin (ear bearing 4.0 MPa at 1.5 m/s, ESTIMATE)

proposed_param_updates.HEEL_REACH_reason: new: longest heel that keeps MIN_WALL of hub over the 8 mm bore

proposed_param_updates.HEEL_W_reason: new: heel width along the pin

GL40 (hardware-study pick) stays the recommended motor. The hardware study's L33 reserve would cut the span to 23.0 mm (< 32)
proposed_param_updates.ORING_EQUATOR_reason: the hardware study's final pick, adopted as is: ISO 3601 / AS568 -141, groove bottom D59.88 (stretch 2.5 %), bore D64.09, spigot OD 63.89, bottom width 2.90 with a 45 deg tip-side flank (top 4.905); the bore fits the wall limit D64.97 (2.44 mm of shell under the 3.0 mm deep pockets at the joint); recomputed here: squeeze 18.7 % nominal, 7.7-29.0 % worst, fill 63.4 % nominal, 79.7 % worst
proposed_param_updates.BAYONET_reason: 3 x 16 deg lugs locked at theta 72.0/192.0/312.0, 35 deg twist; the twist channel stays 10.6 mm clear of the asymmetric pockets; lug shear util 0.17 at the tow design load
proposed_param_updates.FIN_reason: smallest tip-to-tip fin pair whose couple at 1.5 m/s is 1.110 x the CubeMars GL40 KV70 load-line torque (0.1764 N m at TSR 5.75; 10 % margin) with CL <= 0.75 CLmax_3D, and whose YAWED rail pads (pad yawed with the fin about the pivot at 0.15 c, TE toward -theta) clear the pockets; fins on the front shell (TE x 55.5) at theta 93/273, pad-to-pocket 2.22 mm; blades folding at the stowing index clear pads and fins by 3.09 mm. The any-azimuth fold-torus rule would force 25 x 85 fins at x 5.0-29.7, 251 mm tip to tip

proposed_param_updates.POCKETS_reason: rotor half: pocket tables, printable floor (<= 45 deg) and asymmetric azimuth span
proposed_param_updates.BLADE_AXIS_reason: rotor half: solved hull-following pitch axis the blade CAD sweeps along
proposed_param_updates.LIP_SEAL_reason: TC 8x16x5 in the 688's 16 mm bore, 0.5 mm recessed from the static tail end, 1.1 mm ahead of the hub front

The x 12 boss ran into the carrier; the x 6 boss hung in the cavity

proposed_param_updates.POCKET_FLOOR_WALL_reason: new: shell under every pocket floor used by the internal parts (2.0, stricter than the rotor keep-out at MIN_WALL)

resolved_conflicts: Internal layout now reads the real rotor tables (pocket depth / floor / keep-out / azimuth extent, blade axis, hub stations) through hydroegg.layout; the fallback pockets are gone.
STATIC_TAIL_X 118 -> 108: bearings and seal moved 10 mm forward; the bay moved forward and shrank to L 24 so the bearing span stays >= 32 mm.

Pockets crossing the equator: 3.0 mm deep there (not 6), so the joint grew (-141, seal bore D64.09); the socket keeps 2.44 mm under the pocket floor and the lugs sit in the lands (10.6 mm channel clearance).
Hub / bearing / seal axial overlap: none (seal ends x 107.5, hub starts x 108.6); shaft end = hub aft face x 128.0; the tail end block carries the stowed-detent magnet seats.
Fins: with the new hinge (116, 14) the any-azimuth fold torus limits the fin TE to x 31; fins now follow the stowing-index rule and sit at theta 93 / 273.

Review fix round: the fin rail pads are modelled yawed with the fins (pivot 0.15 c, planar pad walls) in the selection, the pocket-clearance and the fold-clearance checks, and run to the equator face; the gland seat moved to x 8.75 on a raised block with no boss in the nose cavity (block, bore and cable exit checked against the carrier and its ring, printable nose-up); buoyancy counts the hub/spinner slots, the spinner access bore and the pads; claw B steps to OD 20 at the tube mouth; the bay is the largest envelope (D50.5 x L24, carrier ring included) and candidate fits are tested against it; the pocket floors are printable (<= 45 deg); the end-view figures say 'seen from aft, looking upstream'.

Fix round completion: the equator joint adopts the hardware study's ISO 3601 / AS568 -141 (bore D64.09, groove bottom D59.88, spigot OD 63.89, 45 deg tip-side flank, top width 4.905), recomputed with the corrected worst case (squeeze 7.7-29.0 %, fill 79.7 %); the fins are re-sized on the CubeMars GL40 KV70 load line (0.1764 N m at TSR 5.75, 1.5 m/s) with a 10 % margin: 40 x 65 mm at 12.00 deg, 219 mm tip to tip (the Cp 0.35 / TSR 4 rule gave 0.282 N m, 1.60 x the load-line torque).
open_issues: Bearing span 32.0 mm against a 37.8 mm overhang to the rotor thrust centroid (x 136.3 on the solved blade axis at 0.7 R): span/overhang 0.85, below the 1.25 rule of thumb. Explicit checks pass (tip runout 0.30 mm, shaft deflection 0.015 mm, s0 >= 22), but measure rotor wobble on the prototype. Only the rotor side could restore the ratio (a longer static tail), and its hinge sweep rejects STATIC_TAIL_X 110 (root clearance 0.77 < 0.8 mm).
Bay length: the bay is D50.5 x L24 (largest that fits). The hardware study's L33 reserve (GM4108H encoder variant, GL40 II, GBM4114HS) does not fit with a 32 mm span; it would leave 23.0 mm.

Roll: the fins carry the mean torque but nothing restores roll angle (pendulum 0.0002 N m vs Q 0.176 N m at 1.5 m/s). If the models are exact, the fin couple is +11 % of Q at 1.5 m/s (hull rolls 5.0 rpm against the rotor), -11 % at 1.0 m/s (3.7 rpm with the rotor) and +18 % at 2.5 m/s (13.4 rpm against the rotor). v2 needs a bridle on two nose eyes (heel 8.4 deg at 1.5 m/s) or a cable swivel; trim fins (+-1 deg) set the balance after the first wet test.

Fins: 219 mm tip to tip (rotor 194 mm), removable for transport. They clear the blades only when the blades fold at the stowing index; folding at another rotor azimuth with the fins on can touch a fin (assembly guide: index the rotor, or remove the fins, before folding). Margins: yawed pad to pocket 2.22 mm, folding blades to pad 3.09 mm and to fin 8.44 mm (limits 2.0); the pad footprint, the pocket raster and the fold sweep (1 deg steps) are sampled, so confirm them on the CAD.
v2 buoyancy: net +0.05 N without ballast (blade slots, spinner access bore and gap counted wet); reaching +0.3 N needs 25 g less mass (4-perimeter shells save 22 g) or ~26 cc of external float.
O-ring worst-case squeeze 8 % is below the 14 % table minimum (print error + full eccentricity); fine at < 0.1 bar, verify with a printed test ring.
Assembly flags: shaft flat passing the lip seal (sleeve), blind claw engagement on closing.

Gland seat: no boss may hang in the nose cavity (the front shell prints nose-up), so the M12 seat is a raised D18 block whose rim stands 6.8 mm proud of the nose; the tapped thread keeps 6.05 of 8 mm in printed material (block, wall, infilled plug with perimeters around the bore). Tap after printing and check the gland's tightening on a test print.
Lug and lip shear use the interlayer tensile adhesion as a proxy (shear strength across layers not sourced); utilisation 0.17.
Hull drag C_D 0.10, radial rotor load 10 % of thrust, one blade 20 % off its share, thrust centroid at 0.7 R: ESTIMATES.

BEM layout_axis_check flew the final blade on hinge (116, 14) and the solved curved axis: cp peak 0.3802 vs 0.3804 nominal, max flap moment 1.343 vs 1.269 Nm at 2.5 m/s (+5.8 %), used for the hub load cases. blade_design.json rotor block still lists hinge (124, 18.5) until params.py adopts the proposed values; the in-plane lead is still ignored there. The rotor load plane used by the bearing checks (x 136.3) is the solved axis at 0.7 R (ESTIMATE), not a BEM thrust centroid.

In-plane lead (pitch axis toward the LE, 11.5 mm at the root to 4.8 mm at the tip) yaws the sections by up to 21 deg against the local tangential flow (rotor.stowed_sections.yaw_vs_local_tangent_deg); BEM assumes 0.
Magnet forces come from a model scaled to catalogue pull (k 0.63); the stowed hold (25.8 N mm) may stop the flow from opening the blades. Verify both detents on a test print.
Pin 3 x 22 (ISO 8734): check stock; fallback 3 x 20 with 2.7 mm ears.
Hub wall over the shaft bore is exactly MIN_WALL (1.24 mm) in the three heel slots (x 114-122).
Rotor loads (stop 237 N, pin shear 18.4 MPa, ear bearing 11.7 MPa at 2.5 m/s) are first-order ESTIMATES; printed PETG allowables were not sourced for them.
Stowed, the section tops are flush but the outer LE/TE edges sit 1.0-1.6 mm below the hull: a visible recess, accepted.
